cover: AI agent or plain automation? Four questions

slides.title: Can you write the rules down?
slides.body: If the person doing the job explains it as a list of conditions, that's automation. "It depends, you just have to read it" is where AI fits.

slides.title: How varied are the inputs?
slides.body: Forms and spreadsheets rarely need a model. Free text, photos and documents often do, but only to turn them into structured data.

slides.title: What does a mistake cost?
slides.body: A model can be right for weeks and then wrong in a way nobody predicted. Expensive actions need a person to approve them.

slides.title: Does the path change case by case?
slides.body: If each case means looking something up and deciding what to check next, an agent may fit. Same five steps every time? It doesn't.

slides.title: Often the answer is one AI step
slides.body: Ordinary automation runs the process, and a model handles the one part a rule can't, like reading a messy request.
